name: Propylene glycol 25%

sources.title: Engineering ToolBox: propylene glycol based heat-transfer fluids

summary: Water with 25% propylene glycol and inhibitors, the usual technical-loop fluid for cold-plate racks (NVIDIA and OCP specify PG25). It resists biological growth and freezing to about -10 °C at a 5% loss of heat capacity.

cpJPerKgK.note: Interpolated between 20% (0.960 Btu/lb°F = 4019) and 30% by mass (0.935 = 3915): 3967 at 25% by mass; PG25 by volume is ~26% by mass and cp falls slightly at lower temperatures.

densityKgM3.note: Interpolated from 1014 (20%) and 1022 (30%) kg/m³ at 20 °C; ~1007 at 40 °C.

viscosityPaS.note: About 2.4 mPa·s at 20 °C and 1.6 mPa·s at 35 °C for 25% PG (ASHRAE Fundamentals glycol tables); not on the ToolBox page.
